answer: An auditor observes each orchard marketplace issuing one ivory credential per identity, priced at 120 POA and burned at registration; the credential embeds a secure-element key that cannot be cloned or reset. Protocol enforcement is direct: any agent whose credential fails the zenith random re-attestation each epoch is barred from payout until it passes. A farm of k identities therefore pays k burns, holds k uncloneable keys and answers k live probes per epoch, so marginal cost stays linear in n while every violation is recorded as an on-ledger slashing.
